listening.title: Asking Good Questions at the End of an Interview

lines.speaker: Hằng (Interviewer)
lines.text: Sơn, we're near the end of the interview. Do you have any questions for me?

lines.speaker: Sơn (Candidate)
lines.text: Yes, thank you. I'd like to ask a thoughtful question about the team first.

lines.speaker: Sơn (Candidate)
lines.text: What does a typical day in the life look like for this role?

lines.speaker: Hằng (Interviewer)
lines.text: You'd usually start with a stand-up, then work on tickets and code reviews.

lines.speaker: Sơn (Candidate)
lines.text: That's helpful. Could I also ask a clarifying question about the advancement opportunity here?

lines.speaker: Hằng (Interviewer)
lines.text: Of course. We support internal promotions and upskilling programs.

lines.speaker: Sơn (Candidate)
lines.text: Great. What career progression could someone in this role expect over time?

lines.speaker: Hằng (Interviewer)
lines.text: Many engineers move into a tech lead or senior role within two years.

lines.speaker: Sơn (Candidate)
lines.text: That sounds promising. What's the leadership style like on this team?

lines.speaker: Hằng (Interviewer)
lines.text: It's fairly hands-off, but we check in every week.

lines.speaker: Sơn (Candidate)
lines.text: Thank you. One last question — what's the decision timeline for this position?
